messages.author: b626043332ddc0cd
messages.subject: Issues with random effects in procD.lm
parts:
Dear all,

I am having some issues with getting my procD.lm models to successfully run and give proper estimates. I am trying to test whether or not there is a difference between the shape of the left and right claws of crayfishes (each crayfish has 2 claws). Normally, I would do this in lme4 by testing (shape ~ claw.side + (1| crayfish.id)). Crayfish.id is the random effect that I want in my model. Each crayfish has two shape observations in my data set, one for the left claw and one for the right claw (i..e, the claw side variable). 

I have tried multiple different syntax's trying to get the model to run, but each time the summary comes out with very strange (incorrect) estimates. 

Below are some of the examples that I have tried, with the model summaries included.

model1<- procD.lm(coords~ csize + crayfish.id + claw.side/crayfish.id, data=agdt,RRPP=T,iter=9999)

summary(model1)
                                              Df      SS   MS     Rsq  F  Z Pr(>F)
claw.side                             1 0.00988    0 0.01660  0  0 0.5005
csize                                     1 0.03835    0 0.06441  0  0 0.5005
claw.side:crayfish.id       209 0.54707    0 0.91899  0  0 0.5005
Residuals                              0 0.00000 -Inf 0.00000            
Total                                    211 0.59530    

model2<- procD.lm(coords ~ claw.side/crayfish.id, data=agdt,RRPP=T,iter=9999)

summary(model2)
                                              Df      SS        MS    Rsq   F   Z Pr(>F)
claw.side                               1 0.00988 0.0098820 0.0166 NaN   0 1.0000
claw.side:crayfish.id          210 0.58542 0.0027877 0.9834 NaN NaN 0.9921
Residuals                              0 0.00000       NaN 0.0000              
Total                                     211 0.59530  

I believe that there are issues with how I am coding my random effect, because the models seem to run fine when I take out the crayfish.id variable. If anyone has any advice that would be great. 

Thanks!
Zack

csize is the centroid cycle calculated from the generalized procrustes analysis. Ideally, I would like to also add in that variable for each claw.

Zach,

 

Check out the ‘bilat.symmetry’ function. This function runs things essentially as a mixed model, allowing for the random effect.

Zach,

 

Your interpretation of the results is correct (and yes, perhaps a bit surprising).

 

Re average shape/size. Yes!  The bilat.symmetry function is commonly used to obtain average L/R shapes. See the $symm.shape component of the output object.
